name: vintage_3mt
source: racing_game-owned vintage 3-speed sliding-mesh manual for the Runabout T (car_runabout), an invented design in the manner of 1910s-1920s three-speed boxes, NOT a specific gearbox [AS]. Ratios 3.60 / 1.90 / 1.00 (direct top) and reverse -4.50 are typical of the period's three-speed boxes behind a long-stroke side-valve four [AS]. Straight-cut sliding gears churn more than a modern helical box: mesh efficiency 0.93 / 0.95 / 0.985 (direct top gear passes through no mesh, only bearing loss) [AS]. A sliding-mesh box has no synchronisers: the small forward 'synchro' capacities (18 / 14 / 12 N*m) are a stand-in for the gear-tooth chamfer and the brake friction a driver uses to match speeds, and the wide dog window (12 rad/s) lets a careful shift engage; a careless one grinds (grind_after_s 0.35). Heavy cast-iron shafts and gears: inertias about twice the economy 5-speed's [AS]. Slow shifts: neutral phase 0.18 s. Torque rating 160 N*m is kept in data/gearboxes/gearbox_catalog.json.
